title: mail send pushes a commit with no message file and still says sent
why: A message that is lost while the sender reads "sent" breaks the mailbox route the owner ruled for every message (page item 482).
note: Filed by triage 11:03 CST Nov 10 from the session-messaging topic session (11:07 CST, its clock). Evidence: on refs/heads/mail of shivinate7/session-mailbox, commit 587de9e ("mail ea1acdfaea67", author ssemwal-cdc, 11:00:59 CST Nov 10) has the same tree as its parent 207a2b1, and the message file for id ea1acdfaea67 is in no folder, open or done. So the login and the push worked from the owner's computer, but the send lost its file. Origin: the owner's card "Test mailbox login on this computer" sent one inform to cloud/session_013NEJL1YBVqsXRPBac7nRcz. Unknown: which computer (Mac or Windows), what it printed, and whether it printed "sent". Done when: the cause is found, a red test shows it, and a fix lands; a send that writes no file prints "not sent", never "sent". Freeze: a fix of an item on main (#2484 session mailbox, merged in batch 71) may run; the coordinator decides. Measured on Windows (session-messaging topic session, 11:12 CST Nov 10; the owner pasted it from his card session). The PC runs Windows 11 Enterprise, hostname ssem-dpromax16. gh holds two accounts: shivinate7 is active and git uses it; the git author is ssemwal-cdc. ls-remote of the mailbox with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 exited 0 in 1.1 s with no prompt and printed refs/heads/mail at 207a2b16ee33, so Windows login works. `mail send --kind inform` exited 0 and printed "sent ea1acdfaea67", but its commit 587de9e has the same tree as its parent, so the message was lost. First guess, unmeasured: hooks/mail.py commit_tree feeds update-index --indexCause: unmeasured. The line-ending guess is refuted (topic session 11:20 CST, its clock): on Linux git, an update-index --index-info line ending in "\r\n" exits 0 and adds the path with a trailing CR, so the tree changes; commit 587de9e kept its parent's tree, so update-index got no entries or did not run as expected. hooks/_nowindow.py passes input= through unchanged. ail.py runs only in the Linux CI job (PR #1371), so no Windows case guards this. Done check: a Windows test reads the pushed tree back, and `mail send` prints "not sent" when the file is missing. The topic session calls this step mailbox-send-empty-commit. Doing 11:10 CST Nov 10: runs as agents in the session-messaging topic session session_013NEJL1YBVqsXRPBac7nRcz (owner chat 11:04 CST: "the fix can run within this session as an agent if anything rather than spawning a lane"); lane [ended:lane:-mail-send-no-file] is archived. Plan: (1) a red test on Linux where the git helper drops stdin, so `mail send` prints "not sent" and exits 1; (2) a read-back check in send; (3) test_mail.py in a Windows CI job, to show the real cause; (4) the owner reruns the card on ssem-dpromax16 after the merge. Round trip test, 2026-11-11 (retrospective 12:25 CST, owner ran the Windows end at the owner's 11:57 CST ask): PC ssem-dpromax16, 5 sends of mail.cmd exit 0 and print "sent"; 0 of 5 stored (ids 012768b42260, 55613ce451b5, 065b36e4e196, 438e3f771c6c, d8cdac4d9178); each pushed a "mail <id>" commit with no file. With 587de9e: 6 of 6 Windows sends lost, silent. Mac send 08c14103ba2b and cloud sends stored. Windows-only and deterministic. Priority raised: first after the drain. Route: a Windows session finds the cause read-only; the fix lands in this lane with a red case first. Cause (owner's Windows session, read-only, relayed 12:27-12:28 CST): hooks/mail.py git() (line 52) runs subprocess.run with text=True, so Windows writes each newline as CRLF. update-index --index-info then gets a path that ends in a carriage return; core.protectNTFS prints "Ignoring path" and exits 0, so must() sees no error; the commit is empty and the push succeeds. hash-object --stdin bodies also get CRLF. The removes list uses the same call, so a Windows take is lost too. Fix: pass stdin as bytes, or newline="\n". Red cases: an --index-info call fails on any "Ignoring path" in stderr; run hooks/test_mail.py on the Windows CI job (today Linux only, checks.yml:213). Guard: the Windows mail suite in CI. A fix of landed code, so R23 allows it. Round trip, 12:30 CST (retrospective): cloud to Windows 5 of 5 stored and listed (ids 77468022b97b, 971e6b628092, 8261607dbfc7, 5c06b13d38b1, 4abc3b67dc6e); Windows to cloud 0 of 5. A Windows take of 77468022b97b printed "taken" and pushed empty commit 5a35caab8; the file stays under mail/, so the take loss is confirmed. After the fix lands: the Windows session takes those 5 messages, and one Windows round trip is the lane's proof.
